draft.title: Greek gods and legacy
card: Ancient Greeks were polytheistic: they worshipped many gods. Zeus was the king of the gods and ruled the sky. Athena was the goddess of wisdom and war, and Athens was named after her.
Greeks honoured their gods with temples, offerings and festivals. The Parthenon in Athens was a temple to Athena.
The Olympic Games began as a festival to honour Zeus. Athletes from many Greek city-states competed at Olympia, and wars were paused so people could travel there safely.

Greece also left ideas that are still used. Philosophers such as Socrates and Plato asked questions about how to live and how to govern. Greek theatre created tragedy and comedy. Many countries today also use democracy, an idea first tried in Greece.
draft.remember: Greeks honoured many gods at temples and festivals, and their ideas in philosophy, theatre and democracy are still used today.

a.q: Why were the Olympic Games held at Olympia in ancient Greece?
opts: They were a festival to honour the god Zeus
They were a training camp for Athenian soldiers
They were a market for trading goods between colonies
They were a meeting to pass laws for all of Greece
a.why: The Games began as a religious festival for Zeus, and athletes from many city-states took part. They were not a military camp or a lawmaking meeting, even though sport and gathering were part of the event.
a.clue: Think about who the festival was meant to honour.

b.q: A museum in Melbourne shows a Greek play, a temple to Athena and a talk by Plato. Which statement best explains why these are still studied today?
opts: Greek ideas in theatre and thought still shape our world
Greece is the only ancient society that kept written records
Greek city-states all shared one religion and one government
Modern countries copied the Greek gods and the laws of Zeus
b.why: The play, temple and philosophy show Greek ideas that still influence the world, such as theatre and philosophy. The other options are wrong: the Greeks were split into independent city-states, and the gods are not used as modern law.
b.clue: Look for the option that links the past to life today.

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about who the festival was meant to honour' gives the answer away: only one option mentions a festival or honouring anyone.

'Why were the Olympic Games held at Olympia' can be read as asking why that place was chosen, but the options answer why the Games were held at all. 'Why were the Olympic Games held in ancient Greece?' would be clearer.

The right option is the only one that echoes 'still' and 'today' from the question, and the clue 'links the past to life today' points straight to it, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

'Athens was named after her' states a myth as fact. Many historians think the goddess's name may come from the city, not the reverse. Something like 'Greeks said Athens was named after her' would be safer.
'Wars were paused' overstates the Olympic truce. It protected people travelling to and from the Games, but it did not stop all wars between city-states.

a.q: Why were the Olympic Games held in ancient Greece?
opts: To honour Zeus, the king of the gods
To honour Athena, the goddess of Athens
To train soldiers for the army of Sparta
To pass laws for all the Greek city-states
a.why: The Games began as a religious festival for Zeus, with athletes from many city-states. Athena was honoured at the Parthenon in Athens, but the Olympic Games were held for Zeus.
a.clue: Think about which god ruled over all the others.

b.q: A Melbourne school stages a tragedy, debates a question Plato asked, and holds a class vote. What does this show?
opts: Greek ideas in theatre, philosophy and democracy live on
These ideas began in Rome and only later reached Greece
Greek ideas were lost once the Greek city-states fell
The Olympic Games are the only Greek idea that lasted
b.why: Tragedy comes from Greek theatre, Plato was a Greek philosopher, and voting reflects democracy, first tried in Greece. The Rome option is tempting, but these ideas began in Greece, not Rome.
b.clue: Match each activity to an area of Greek life.
